thread:
maria: Suggest we deprioritize the 'edge network presets' work for Q2. Field asks are noisy but the engineering cost and ongoing maintenance looks disproportionate.
aj: Can you share the numbers? how many customers actually use the presets today?
tara: worried about downstream impact — a lot of sales folks have promised 'one-click' onramp to netops teams. if we pull it we need a clear comms/migration plan.
maria: Agreed re: comms. Quick summary: 7 active customers asked for presets in last 6 months, 3 of those were pilot-only. Engineering estimate: ~4 dev-months + 0.5 dev-month/quarter for support/bugfixes.
kevin: 4 dev-months seems low for all the edge cases (multi-VPC, NAT, egress IP preservation). what's the risk if we move to 'template + docs' instead of shipped presets?
samir: Metric-wise: only 2 customers have hit the preset path in production; rest are proofs. ROI is low. Also, presets increase our test matrix (operator + network combos).
aj: If we don't ship presets, can we still offer a concierge implementation for top-tier customers?
maria: Yes — proposal: deprioritize building baked presets in the installer, but create a supported concierge playbook and a set of reference templates in the docs repo. That reduces code surface and still supports enterprise deals. :thumbsup:
tara: For launch readiness, we should define clear acceptance criteria for the templates: example topologies, BGP/peering notes, egress IP examples, and a minimal validation checklist ops can run.
kevin: Also add an 'upgrade path' doc: how to move from templates -> operator-managed presets later if we decide to re-prioritize. include rollback steps and a small script to validate IP preservation.
ops-bot: deploy-stats: past 30 days: private deployments with custom net configs = 18, automated preset usage = 2, failed installs due to network = 1.
elena: Sales concern: some deals are contingent on baked-in onramp. If we move to concierge + templates, we need a packaging SLA and a pricing clause. otherwise legal will object.
maria: noted. Proposed next steps: 1) create template repo PR (owner: kevin) 2) concierge offering doc for sales (owner: elena) 3) validation checklist and small validation script (owner: tara) 4) update installer roadmap to mark presets deferred (owner: aj).
kevin: I'll start the template PR this week. plan: include 3 reference topologies (single-VPC, peered-VPC, on-prem relay) + a simple egress-preserve script.
tara: I'll draft the validation checklist and include the minimal k8s/net commands and a smoke test.
elena: I'll talk to sales about a short-term SLA and pricing band. if needed we can offer a 30-day concierge window for high-value deals.
aj: I'll update the roadmap doc and internal notes, call the feature 'edge-net-presets (deferred) — templates + concierge alternative'.
samir: Suggest adding a small telemetry flag so we can track template adoption vs bespoke installs. helps inform re-prioritization later.
maria: Good call. add telemetry flag to template README and to the concierge playbook. we'll revisit in 6 weeks with adoption metrics.
tara: one more: docs need a clear 'compatibility matrix' for operator versions + installer. I'll include that in the PR.
kevin: timeline check — PR by Thu, checklist by Fri, concierge doc next Tue, roadmap updated today.
elena: I'll sync with legal on pricing language tomorrow.
maria: action items captured. thanks all. tagging re-review in 6 weeks. :spiral_calendar:
